newsitem.title: ITALY: Generali to create $12 mln holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Generali to create $12 mln holocaust fund.

text.p: Italian insurer Generali said on Tuesday that it was setting up a fund of $12 million to honour the victims of the holocaust, with this money to be paid out over the next 12 years to organisations supporting victims.
In a company statement, Generali added that it would also set up a centre in the next few weeks to give out information to holocaust victims.

But Generali continued to stand by its declaration of earlier this year that it could not be held responsible after so many years as other organisations had taken over its operations in Eastern European countries with the advent of communist regimes and it is to them that any claims should be made.
Generali added that it had not been able to give evidence to the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, where Generali has been criticised for lack of action towards holocaust victims.

Generali added that its chairman Antoine Bernheim and managing director Gianfranco Gutty plan to visit Israel in July. Earlier this year, Generali invested $320 million to acquire a majority stake in Israeli insurer Migdal, the insurance arm of Israeli government-owned Bank Leumi.
